key_insight: Low-Reynolds-number propeller speed changes can produce thrust hysteresis even when rotor-disk inflow, blade deformation, and sectional circulation remain largely quasi-steady.
engineering_relevance: Steady thrust maps may misestimate transient thrust during rapid speed commands in small UAVs, with implications for control accuracy.
method: Tested a two-bladed propeller in hover at pitch offsets of 0°, 5°, and 10°.
Applied open-loop acceleration and deceleration steps between 3000 and 5000 RPM.
Combined load measurements with phase-locked PIV at 40%, 60%, and 80% rotor radius and in the meridian plane.
evidence_signal: At the 5° pitch offset, thrust-coefficient deviations reached 8% during acceleration and 5% during deceleration; flow-field departures were greatest at low rotational speeds rather than peak acceleration.
watch_item: The abstract inconsistently describes the 10° case as both quasi-steady and exhibiting deviations; verify pitch-dependent conclusions in the full paper before implementation.
paper_title: On the aerodynamics of an accelerating and decelerating propeller in hover at low Reynolds numbers
